docs.title: CrystaLLM for NOMAD
docs.text:
Generate candidate crystal structures from chemical compositions and save the CIF files and result entries in your NOMAD project.

Use CrystaLLM on NOMAD Oasis.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Follow Using the action form to enter a composition, choose inference settings, and run the action. The same guide covers multiple prompts, CSV/XLSX tables, and downloading results.

  • Installation and Oasis setup is for administrators adding the plugin to a deployment.
  • Contributing covers local development, tests, and documentation previews.

docs.title: Contribute to this plugin
docs.text: For everyday use, see Using the action form. Deployment administrators can follow Installation.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
For contributing to the plugin, clone the repository and install its development dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-crystallm.git
cd nomad-crystallm
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install uv
uv pip install -e '.[dev]'

docs.title: Developing on nomad-distro-dev
docs.text:
Use the dedicated nomad-distro-dev workspace when developing against local NOMAD packages. Add the plugin to its root dependencies with the cpu-action extra:

dependencies = [
  # Other workspace dependencies...
  "nomad-crystallm[cpu-action]",
]

Follow the workspace README to configure its infrastructure, including Temporal. Use compatible NOMAD and UI revisions with action-form support. From the workspace root, run its setup task:

uv run poe setup

Then start these services in separate terminals. Run the API and CPU action worker commands from the workspace root:

uv run poe start

uv run poe cpuworker

Start the UI with action forms from the workspace's ui directory:

cd ui
npm install
npm start

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
From the plugin directory:

python -m pytest -sv tests

To generate a coverage report:

uv pip install pytest-cov
python -m pytest --cov=src tests

docs.title: Run linting and auto-formatting
docs.text:
ruff check .
ruff format . --check

Run ruff format . to apply formatting changes.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
Use python -m pytest --pdb tests to stop on a failing test. For VS Code, adapt this configuration in .vscode/launch.json to the test you want to inspect:

{
  "configurations": [
    {
      "name": "Debug plugin tests",
      "type": "debugpy",
      "request": "launch",
      "program": "${workspaceFolder}/.venv/bin/pytest",
      "args": ["-sv", "--pdb", "tests/test_inference_generation.py"],
      "justMyCode": true
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Documentation on Github pages
docs.text:
From the plugin directory:

uv pip install -r requirements_docs.txt
mkdocs serve

docs.title: Template update
docs.text: Plugin maintainers can use cruft to check for updates to the project template. Run cruft update from the plugin repository. Oasis administrators and action-form users do not need this step.

docs.title: Install and configure the plugin
docs.text: This page is for Oasis administrators and local installations. If CrystaLLM is already available on your deployment, follow Using the action form.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Use the Python environment or custom container image of your NOMAD deployment. The package requires nomad-lab>=2.0.0 and a NOMAD UI with action forms. Use a Python version supported by your NOMAD installation.

Install the plugin with its inference dependencies:

python -m pip install 'nomad-crystallm[cpu-action]'

For an installation using the repository version of the plugin:

python -m pip install 'nomad-crystallm[cpu-action] @ git+https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/nomad-crystallm.git'

Use the same plugin version in the API and action-worker environments. Installing nomad-crystallm without the cpu-action extra provides the schema dependencies but does not install everything needed to run inference.

Installing the Python package alone does not start an Oasis or an inference worker. Complete the setup below before running an action.

docs.title: Adding this plugin to NOMAD
docs.text:
Choose the subsection matching your installation:

  1. An existing NOMAD Oasis.
  2. A local NOMAD installation.

docs.title: Adding this plugin in your NOMAD Oasis
docs.text:
1. Add nomad-crystallm[cpu-action] to your deployment's package requirements or custom NOMAD image. Rebuild and redeploy the services that use that image; installing into a running container alone will not survive its replacement.
  2. Make sure your deployment runs Temporal and that NOMAD can connect to it. Merge the following into nomad.yaml, using your deployment's Temporal host and namespace:
temporal:
  enabled: true
  host: temporal
  port: 7233
  namespace: default

Here, temporal is an example container service name. For a native local installation, the host may be localhost.

  1. Run a NOMAD CPU action worker with the plugin installed, the same NOMAD configuration as the API, and access to the deployment's upload and action storage:
nomad admin run action-cpu-worker

For a container deployment, run this as a worker service using the configured NOMAD image and storage mounts. The action uses the CPU task queue; PyTorch uses CUDA when it is available to that worker and otherwise runs on CPU.

  1. Give the worker access to download the model from Zenodo on its first run. Keep its action-artifact storage persistent so later runs can reuse the downloaded model.
  2. Restart the API and CPU action worker after installing or updating the plugin. Sign in to the UI and check that CrystaLLM Inference appears under Run action. If your deployment restricts plugin entry points, allow nomad_crystallm.actions.inference:crystallm_inference and nomad_crystallm.schemas:crystallm_schemas.

For deployments with prompt-table upload support, also merge the following into nomad.yaml. This preserves the default Action Assets file types and adds CSV and XLSX; retain any additional types your deployment already allows.

actions:
  action_assets:
    allowed_media_types:
      - audio/*
      - image/*
      - application/pdf
      - application/json
      - text/plain
      - application/octet-stream
      - text/csv
      - application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet

Restart the API and worker after changing the configuration. See the NOMAD Oasis plugin configuration documentation for deployment-specific plugin setup.

docs.title: Adding this plugin in your local NOMAD installation and the source code of NOMAD
docs.text:
Install the package in the environment used by your local NOMAD API and CPU action worker, then apply the Temporal and storage setup above.

For development across NOMAD and the plugin, use nomad-distro-dev. See Developing on nomad-distro-dev below for the workspace setup and service commands.

docs.title: Using the action form
docs.text: Open NOMAD Oasis and sign in to run CrystaLLM Inference. You do not need to install the package on your own computer.

docs.title: Start with one composition
docs.text:
1. Open or create an unpublished project where you have permission to add files.
  2. Choose Run action from the project, then select CrystaLLM Inference. You can also start from Run action on the NOMAD Actions page.
  3. Check Upload Id. It is pre-filled when you open the form from a project; otherwise enter the destination project's upload ID.
  4. Under Prompt Construction Inputs, add an item:
Field Example Meaning Composition NaCl Chemical formula to generate a structure for. Num Formula Units Per Cell 1 Number of reduced formula units in the cell; choose 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, or 8. Space Group Leave empty Optionally constrain generation to a space group from the list.
  1. Under Inference Settings, keep crystallm_v1_small and one sample for a first run. The settings are explained below.
  2. Choose Run, then follow View action in the confirmation message. You can return to the run through Action History on the NOMAD Actions page.

The first run can take longer while the worker downloads the model. Follow the status and available activity logs on the action's details page.

docs.title: Run multiple prompts
docs.text: Add more items under Prompt Construction Inputs to run several compositions in one action. Each item has its own formula-unit count and optional space group. Num Samples applies to every prompt: three prompts with two samples each produce six generated CIFs.

docs.title: Uploading prompt tables
docs.text:
Use Prompts File to choose a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file, either alone or alongside manual inputs. Valid file rows are appended after the manual inputs, in file order, without removing duplicates.

If Prompts File is missing, use manual inputs or ask your administrator to install a plugin version with table-upload support.

Use these columns in this order; the header row is optional:

composition,num_formula_units_per_cell,space_group
NaCl,1,
TiO2,2,P 1
Si,8,F d -3 m

Only composition is required. Blank or omitted trailing cells use 1 formula unit and no space-group constraint. Use the same space-group spelling as the form, such as P 1.

Save CSV files as UTF-8. Excel uploads use the first worksheet; .xls files are not supported. Blank rows are ignored, and invalid rows are skipped with their row numbers and reasons recorded in the action logs. At least one valid manual or file prompt must remain. An unreadable or unsupported file fails the action.

The table is a private action attachment; it is not added to your project's raw files. Results are saved in the project selected in Upload Id.

docs.title: Choose inference settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Purpose Model crystallm_v1_small Choose crystallm_v1_large for the larger model, which needs more worker resources and time. Num Samples 1 Generate up to five candidate structures per prompt. Max New Tokens 3000 Limit the generated sequence length; increase if generation stops before completing the structure. Temperature 0.8 Control randomness during token sampling. Top K 10 Limit sampling to this many likely next tokens. Seed 1337 Set the random seed used for inference. Batch Size 16 Control the number of samples passed to inference at once; reduce if the worker runs out of memory.

Leave Dtype (bfloat16) and Compile (off) at their defaults unless you need to adapt inference to your worker's PyTorch and hardware setup. Batch size does not change the requested sample count, and prompts of different lengths can be submitted together.

docs.title: Find and download results
docs.text:
After the action completes, return to the destination project's files and open crystallm_inference_<timestamp>. Each prompt has a numbered subfolder:

crystallm_inference_<timestamp>/
  composition_1_NaCl/
    NaCl_1.cif
    crystallm_NaCl.archive.json

Open the result entry to inspect its material structure, inference settings, and links to the generated CIF samples. Download the CIFs from the project's files. If a generated structure fails processing, inspect its entry processing logs and CIF file.

If the action stays pending or the form does not offer CrystaLLM Inference, ask your administrator to check the installation and CPU action worker. For rejected table uploads, ask them to check the spreadsheet media-type allowlist on that page. Check skipped-row warnings if fewer results appear than expected.
